name: corpus-coverage
title: Corpus Coverage — Full 1,096-Model BioModels Catalog on HRA 3D Anatomy
question:
Of the HRA ASCT+B-3D crosswalk's 1,730 Uberon-keyed anatomical structures
(across 114 source-organ GLBs), how many are covered once every curated
BioModels model — not just a narrow search query — is crossed against
them, and does full-corpus coverage reach organs a single-query search
misses (e.g. kidney)?

study_card.goal: Cross the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk's anatomical structures with the committed full-corpus catalog's organ->models index (1,096 curated BioModels, 82 organ-tagged) and confirm the composite loads a non-empty per-AS coverage list plus summary counts, at full-catalog scale.
study_card.mechanism: CoverageStep.update (catalog_path set) -> build_corpus_coverage(catalog_path) -> load_corpus_catalog(datasets/biomodel_corpus_catalog.json) x fetch_crosswalk(...) -> per-AS `covered` flag (own Uberon has models, or its organ_glb belongs to a covered organ) -> coverage + coverage_summary -> RAMEmitter.
study_card.expected_result: Coverage substantially wider than the 25-result query-scoped model-coverage-3d study — more organs, more AS nodes covered — including kidney, which the narrower glucose-regulation query does not cover.
study_card.main_expert_question: Does full-corpus organ-tagging (82/1,096 models tagged with a resolvable HRA organ) undercount real anatomical relevance — i.e. are many of the untagged 1,014 models actually organ-specific but missed by the current synonym/reference-organ-name matching?

biological_summary:
A single BioModels search query (as in `model-coverage-3d`) only ever
samples the corpus through the lens of its search terms. This study
instead retrieves and organ-tags the full curated BioModels catalog
(1,096 `BIOMD*` models, Task A) and crosses every organ it can tag against
the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk, giving the ceiling on how much of the HRA's
fine-grained 3D anatomy the *entire* published mechanistic-modeling
literature (as indexed by BioModels) actually touches — not just the
glucose-regulation slice. This directly measures how much anatomy is
"dark" (unmodeled) versus "lit" (has at least one curated model),
informing where new HRA-3D coverage work would have the most impact.
readouts: catalog n_ids / n_named / n_tagged (corpus retrieval + organ-tagging yield)

report.title: Corpus Coverage — 635/1,730 AS nodes covered across 31/114 organs, kidney included
report.objective:
Crossing the full 1,096-model curated BioModels catalog against the
ASCT+B-3D crosswalk, how many anatomical structures/organs are covered,
and does it reach organs a narrow query misses?
report.conclusion:
The committed catalog (`datasets/biomodel_corpus_catalog.json`) retrieved
1,096/1,096 curated BioModels IDs, named all 1,096, and organ-tagged
82 (7.5%) against HRA reference-organ names. Crossing that catalog's
organ->models index with the live crosswalk (1,730 Uberon-keyed AS
rows / 114 source-organ GLBs) covers 635 AS nodes (36.7%) across 31
distinct organ GLBs (27.2%) — an order of magnitude wider than the
25-result glucose-regulation query's 58 AS nodes / 4 organs
(`model-coverage-3d`). Critically, kidney is now covered
(`VH_F_Kidney_L`/`_R`, `VH_M_Kidney_L`/`_R`), which the narrower query
missed entirely, confirming full-corpus retrieval finds anatomically
relevant models a single search term does not.
report.caveat:
Organ-tagging yield is low relative to catalog size (82/1,096 = 7.5%
tagged) — the remaining 1,014 models are either genuinely
organ-agnostic (pathway/signaling models with no single anatomical
site) or are organ-specific but missed by the current
synonym/reference-organ-name matching (the study's main expert
question). Coverage is still organ-granularity, not per-AS-node model
matching: a covered organ's Uberon marks every AS node cut from its
GLB as covered, which can overstate coverage for anatomically distinct
sub-structures with no direct model evidence.
